subject: AuroraMed: access control evidence intake
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@auroramed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@auroramed.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraMed SOC2 intake — ask: SAML/SCIM/least-priv artifacts

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. AuroraMed is doing our vendor SOC 2 and SIG intake this week and we need a short package of access-control evidence to close a couple of open items on our end. Can you provide the following by EOD Friday (2026-09-04 PST)? If you need more time, please let us know and propose a new date.

Requested artifacts:
- Sample SAML assertion logs for a typical user login (3–5 examples, timestamps and subject attributes redacted where appropriate).
- A SCIM delta export (last 7 days) showing create/update/delete events (CSV acceptable).
- A current least-privilege mapping for admin/service accounts and role owners (spreadsheet or doc).
- Short notes describing how RBAC is implemented for support/admin roles (one-paragraph).

If there are any data sensitivity concerns, we can accept redacted samples or an on-call Zoom to review logs. We also included the SIG control IDs relevant to access control in the attached intake checklist.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lewis
Senior Vendor Security Manager
AuroraMed

Attachments: AuroraMed_SOC2_intake_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@auroramed.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraMed SOC2 intake — ask: SAML/SCIM/least-priv artifacts

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. We can provide redacted SAML assertion samples and a SCIM delta export. A few clarifying Qs before we pull everything:

1) Scope — do we include system/service accounts (e.g., batch transformers and CI service users) in the least-priv mapping, or only interactive/admin roles?
2) For SAML assertions: do you need full raw XML or is a text dump of the SAML response (with NameID/email and common attributes) sufficient?
3) Are there any specific user IDs you want in the SCIM delta sample, or should we provide a random 7-day slice from production that excludes patient data?

We expect to deliver: a redacted SAML assertion file (text), scim-delta-sample.csv, and a least-privilege spreadsheet. Will confirm when the package is uploaded to a shared drive link.

Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: AuroraMed SOC2 intake — action items and owners

Team — forwarding AuroraMed's intake. Sara asked for SAML samples, SCIM delta (7d), and least-priv mapping. Timeline: EOD Friday PST.

Action items:
- Tessa: please export a SCIM delta CSV covering 2026-08-27 — 2026-09-03 (creates/updates/deletes). Redact any email addresses that look like patient or customer identifiers. Put the file name scim-delta-sample.csv.
- Grace: produce a current least-privilege mapping (least-priv-mapping.xlsx) covering: admin/support roles, service accounts, role owners, and any justifications for elevated rights. Use one worksheet per domain (support, infra, product).
- Both: I will gather SAML assertion samples. For SAML we will provide text dumps of three typical assertions (login, re-auth, and session-restore) with NameID and common attributes; we will remove IP and session IDs. Save SAML samples as saml-assertions-sample.txt (include brief header lines with timestamps).

Compliance notes: Keep the files redacted. Do not include raw logs with PII. Upload to the shared drive folder and post the link back to me; I will send the drive link to AuroraMed's security mailbox.

If either of you anticipate being blocked on redaction or need more time, call me directly.

Thanks — Naomi
